note: Re-judged 2026-11-14 by an independent auditor who authored none of 178cffd97d, 1c6795e9e4, 43cfa9af6e, after session_wedge_test.go::TestHoldExpiryClosesBehindStuckWriter joined the row as a third positive. RFC 4271 Section 8.2.2 (Established) read at rfc/full/rfc4271.txt:3988-4006: "If the HoldTimer_Expires event occurs (Event 10), the local system: - sends a NOTIFICATION message with the Error Code Hold Timer Expired, - sets the ConnectRetryTimer to zero, - releases all BGP resources, - drops the TCP connection,". The new unit drives a real Session to Established over net.Pipe with Run executing (wedgeEstablished), stops the keepalive timer so the hold expiry is the only callback the fake-clock advance runs, takes writeMu as a writer blocked in a socket write holds it, fires the production hold expiry, and requires the peer end to read io.EOF (errors.Is, a timeout is t.Fatal) within holdExpiryNotifyDeadline (1s) plus 2s slack; after the release Run must return ErrHoldTimerExpired and the FSM be Idle. Q1: it asserts the RFC clause "drops the TCP connection" as the peer observes it, not an internal flag. Q2: a close that waits for the write path leaves the pipe open and the select times out; rfc/discrimination/rfc4271/RFC4271-8.2.2-4.json records the red under a disabled dropConn (session_connection.go). Q3: EOF can only come from ze closing its end (the fixture's own close yields io.ErrClosedPipe, which the assertion refuses), and ErrHoldTimerExpired pins the hold expiry as the cause. Q4: the unit proves the drop clause alone, in the one state where the NOTIFICATION cannot be written; its claim says exactly that (EOF within the bound, write path held) and claims neither the NOTIFICATION, the timer nor the release. Those clauses stay with the four earlier units, whose fingerprints did not move: HoldExpiryRunsTheEvent10ActionList and EstablishedHoldTimerExpiryRunsTheEvent10List pin code 4 read from the connection before closure, the timer stops, session release and EOF; NoHoldExpiryLeavesTheSessionIntact and EstablishedHoldTimerFedByKeepalivesNeverExpires are the negatives. Whole requirement enforced across the five. Observation, not a finding against the row: with the write path held no NOTIFICATION reaches the wire, which RFC 4271 cannot require of a socket that accepts no write; the connection drop is what remains owed and is what the unit proves. Native commands were not run by the auditor.
